The evidence suggests that Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside acts as a target for Guanylate cyclase soluble subunit alpha-2, which in turn is targeted by Citrusinol. This chain of targets ultimately leads to the activation of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential role for Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside in modulating the activity of the transporter, possibly through the regulation of downstream targets like Guanylate cyclase soluble subunit alpha-2. The mechanism involves a sequential interaction where the compound may influence the function of the transporter via its effects on intermediate molecules, suggesting a complex regulatory network. The evidence supports a plausible but not definitively established link, emphasizing the need for further experimental validation to confirm the exact nature of the interaction.
